value_stream.name: Merchandise Financial Planning, Open-to-Buy & Margin Management

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Category Managers, BI (links to VS-28.1), Finance (links to VS-17.1)

workflows.name: Weekly Merchandise P&A Reporting & Variance Analysis

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-flag of "flags vs threshold" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-analyze of "analyze variance root cause" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Merchandise Planner consolidate actions and feed to weekly P&A" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-534 (ensure controlled execution — Merchandise Performance Analytics & Margin Optimization (PA-101.3).)
- operational: weekly cadence and automation; operational: disciplined root-cause analysis
Pain Points / Risks: - **Latency risk**: Slow P&A cycle delays corrective action; mitigated by weekly cadence and automation
- **Attribution risk**: Misread variance causes wrong action; mitigated by disciplined root-cause analysis
System Touchpoints: - BI/reporting (links to VS-28.1); merchandise planning; POS/analytics (links to VS-08); GL (links to VS-17.1)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner/BI produce weekly merchandise P&A pack: sales, GM%, receipts, markdowns, EOM stock, sell-through, turn, WOS by department/category vs plan and vs last year; variance flags vs threshold

Category Managers analyze variance root cause (demand, price, mix, stockout, promo, weather per VS-69) and propose corrective action (chase/cancel/markdown/transfer) against OTB (W3283) and markdown budget (W3285)
Merchandise Planner consolidate actions and feed to weekly P&A review (W3288); archive the pack for audit (links to VS-21.1) and trend analysis

fields.Participants: Category Manager, Merchandise Planner, Buyers (links to VS-03), Supply Planning (links to VS-02.1)
fields.Volume: A-items (~20% of SKUs = 80% revenue, per profile §6.6)

workflows.name: Key-Item / Item-Class Performance Review & Reorder/Cancel Decisioning

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "Category Manager review key-item" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-allocate of "Category Manager/Buyers decide chase" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-update of "Merchandise Planner capture decisions, update OTB/commitments" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-534 (ensure controlled execution — Merchandise Performance Analytics & Margin Optimization (PA-101.3).)
- operational: weekly key-item discipline and chase; operational: reforecast (W3288)
Pain Points / Risks: - **A-item stockout risk**: Lost sales on 80%-revenue items; mitigated by weekly key-item discipline and chase
- **Over-chase risk**: Reactive chase creates post-trend overstock; mitigated by reforecast (W3288)
System Touchpoints: - Key-item analytics; PO (links to VS-03.2); demand planning (links to VS-02.1); allocation (links to VS-55)

steps.activity: Category Manager review key-item (A-item) performance: sell-through, stock cover, rate-of-sale, in-stock %, on-order; flag items trending above/below plan

Category Manager/Buyers decide chase (expedite/reorder per VS-03.2), cancel/defer open order, or reallocate (links to VS-55 allocation) within OTB (W3284); coordinate import chase feasibility (45–90d lead per VS-02.2) vs domestic chase
Merchandise Planner capture decisions, update OTB/commitments (W3283/W3284) and reforecast (W3288), and confirm in-stock recovery

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Pricing (links to VS-01.2/VS-57), Category Managers, Finance (links to VS-17.1)
fields.Trigger: Clearance cycle; aged inventory (W3294); margin optimization review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "discount, and coordinate channel execution" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-post of "Merchandise Planner/Finance measure realized markdown margin vs optimized plan" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-534 (ensure controlled execution — Merchandise Performance Analytics & Margin Optimization (PA-101.3).)
- operational: elasticity-based optimization; operational: cadence optimization
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-discount risk**: Markdown deeper than needed destroys margin; mitigated by elasticity-based optimization
- **Under-clearance risk**: Shallow markdown fails to clear, leaving aged stock (W3294); mitigated by cadence optimization
System Touchpoints: - Markdown/price optimization (links to VS-57); price management (links to VS-01.2); clearance (links to VS-64); GL (links to VS-17.1)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner/Pricing run markdown optimization: model demand elasticity and clearance-rate by markdown depth, compute the margin-maximizing markdown cadence and timing to clear within target weeks

Category Managers select markdown depth/round per item within markdown budget (W3285), avoid margin-destructive over-discount, and coordinate channel execution (stores, ecommerce, marketplace links to VS-65/VS-95)
Merchandise Planner/Finance measure realized markdown margin vs optimized plan (W3286), update elasticity model with actuals, and feed learnings to next cycle (links to VS-64.3 post-season analysis)

fields.Frequency: Per promotion (≈6 major + monthly hot deals)
fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Category Managers, Marketing (links to VS-14.1), Pricing (links to VS-57), Loyalty (links to VS-13.2)

workflows.name: Promotion Post-Mortem, Halo & Cannibalization Margin Analysis

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-measure of "measure promotion performance vs plan" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-compile of "compile promo post-mortem, update promo playbooks" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-534 (ensure controlled execution — Merchandise Performance Analytics & Margin Optimization (PA-101.3).)
- operational: halo/cannibalization analysis; operational: rebate recovery (links to VS-39)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cannibalization-blindness risk**: Promo shifts, not grows, sales; mitigated by halo/cannibalization analysis
- **Vendor-funding-leak risk**: Unclaimed co-op erodes promo ROI; mitigated by rebate recovery (links to VS-39)
System Touchpoints: - Promo analytics (links to VS-14.1/VS-58); loyalty (links to VS-13.2); bundle (links to VS-92); BI (links to VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner measure promotion performance vs plan: incremental sales, halo (lift on non-promoted adjacent items), cannibalization (shift from substituted items), margin vs non-promo baseline, and loyalty-member response (links to VS-13.2)

Category Managers/Marketing assess promo ROI (incremental margin − promo cost − vendor funding per VS-39.2), vendor co-op recovery, and customer-acquisition/retention value; compare promo mechanics (price-off, bundle links to VS-92, coupon links to VS-58)
Merchandise Planner compile promo post-mortem, update promo playbooks (links to VS-14.1/VS-58), and feed learnings to the next seasonal plan (W3282) and promo calendar

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Category Managers, Vendor Mgmt (links to VS-03/VS-67), Rebate (links to VS-39), Finance (links to VS-17.1)
fields.Trigger: Quarterly vendor review (links to VS-67); rebate settlement (links to VS-39)

workflows.name: Vendor Margin Contribution, Terms & Rebate Impact Analysis

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Category Managers/Vendor Mgmt evaluate terms" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-identify of "identify consolidation/exit candidates" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-534 (ensure controlled execution — Merchandise Performance Analytics & Margin Optimization (PA-101.3).)
- operational: rebate discipline (links to VS-39); operational: terms-cost modeling
Pain Points / Risks: - **Rebate-leak risk**: Earned rebates not claimed/reconciled; mitigated by rebate discipline (links to VS-39.1)
- **Terms-cost-blindness risk**: Long payment terms carry hidden capital cost; mitigated by terms-cost modeling
System Touchpoints: - Vendor scorecard (links to VS-67); rebate (links to VS-39); AP terms (links to VS-15); GL (links to VS-17.1)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner compute vendor margin contribution (net margin after rebate, terms cost, returns/damage per VS-90, and quality cost per VS-31) and rank vendors by true profitability, not just topline

Category Managers/Vendor Mgmt evaluate terms (payment terms cost-of-capital, discounts), rebate realization (links to VS-39), and vendor-funded programs (links to VS-39.2 co-op, VS-62.2 vendor-funded display); negotiate improvement with low-margin vendors
Merchandise Planner/Finance fold vendor-margin contribution into category margin plan (W3286) and the vendor scorecard (links to VS-67.2); identify consolidation/exit candidates

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Allocation (links to VS-55), Store Ops (links to VS-07), Category Managers

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-file of "Merchandise Planner analyze store/cluster merchandise performance" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-capture of "capture local demand" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report cluster results" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-534 (ensure controlled execution — Merchandise Performance Analytics & Margin Optimization (PA-101.3).)
- operational: variant-count governance caps localization drift; cluster analytics reviewed quarterly
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-localization risk**: Too many cluster variants fragment supply and inflate inventory; mitigated by discipline
- **Missed-local-demand risk**: One-size assortment under-serves clusters; mitigated by cluster analytics
System Touchpoints: - Store/cluster analytics (links to VS-28.1); allocation (links to VS-55); space (links to VS-55.3); POS (links to VS-08)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner analyze store/cluster merchandise performance: sales/sqm, margin, turn, sell-through by cluster (Metro Manila vs provincial, Mindanao vs Luzon per profile §3.1), localize assortment where data supports

Category Managers/Allocation adjust cluster assortment depth/width, allocation (links to VS-55), and pricing (regional price intelligence per VS-57) to capture local demand; manage local/private-label fit (links to VS-41)
Merchandise Planner measure localization lift vs national baseline, balance localization against assortment simplicity and supply efficiency (links to VS-02/VS-04), and report cluster results

fields.Participants: Merchandise Planner, Finance (links to VS-17.1), Internal Audit (links to VS-21.1), VP Merchandising
fields.Trigger: Period-end; internal audit plan (links to VS-21.1)

workflows.name: Markdown/OTB Audit & Merchandise Financial Control Review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "documented and approved, and receipt commitments within OTB" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review merchandise financial controls" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-update of "update controls, and report control effectiveness to VP Merchandising and audit…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-69 (ensure merchandise financial plan & OTB discipline.)
- operational: audit trail and review; operational: control review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Override-abuse risk**: Unauthorized OTB/markdown overrides erode plan discipline; mitigated by audit trail and review
- **Provision-accuracy risk**: Inaccurate markdown/provision distorts financials; mitigated by control review
System Touchpoints: - Merchandise planning audit trail; GL (links to VS-17.1); audit (links to VS-21.1); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner/Finance audit markdown spend authorization and OTB adherence: verify markdowns within budget (W3285), OTB overrides documented and approved, and receipt commitments within OTB (W3283/W3284)

Internal Audit (links to VS-21.1) review merchandise financial controls: plan integrity, override approvals, markdown accuracy, inventory provisioning (W3294), and segregation between planning and execution; test samples
Merchandise Planner/Finance remediate findings, update controls, and report control effectiveness to VP Merchandising and audit committee (links to VS-36)

fields.Participants: VP Merchandising, Merchandise Planners, BI (links to VS-28.1), FP&A (links to VS-17.4), CEO/COO/CFO
fields.Trigger: Monthly executive review; board reporting (links to VS-33.2/VS-36.1)

workflows.name: Merchandise KPI Dashboard, Category Scorecard & Executive Review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "review with Category Managers" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-534 (ensure controlled execution — Merchandise Performance Analytics & Margin Optimization (PA-101.3).)
- operational: balanced scorecard; operational: near-real-time BI (links to VS-28)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Metric-silo risk**: Category scorecards optimized for one metric (e.g., sales) at the expense of margin/turn; mitigated by balanced scorecard
- **Reporting-latency risk**: Stale dashboards mislead decisions; mitigated by near-real-time BI (links to VS-28.1)
System Touchpoints: - BI dashboard (links to VS-28.1); merchandise planning; FP&A (links to VS-17.4); board reporting (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Merchandise Planner/BI maintain the merchandise KPI dashboard and category scorecard: sales, GM%, turn, GMROI, sell-through, in-stock, markdown %, OTB utilization, aged-inventory %, vendor margin, channel mix — vs plan and LY
VP Merchandising conduct monthly category scorecard review with Category Managers; recognize top performers, action underperformers, and reallocate OTB/space (links to VS-55.3) and people focus

VP Merchandising present merchandise results to executive committee and board (links to VS-33.2/VS-36.1): performance vs plan, margin outlook, inventory health, key risks (links to VS-21.2), and strategic recommendations
